What is a hemoglobin A1C (HbA1C) test?
A hemoglobin A1C (HbA1C) test is a blood test that shows your average level of blood glucose, also called blood sugar, over the past two to three months.
An A1C test can show your average glucose level for the past three months because:

Glucose sticks to hemoglobin for as long as the red blood cells are alive.
Red blood cells live about three months.

High A1C levels are a sign of high blood glucose from diabetes.
Other names: HbA1C, A1C, glycohemoglobin, glycated hemoglobin, glycosylated hemoglobinWhat is it used for?
Your blood glucose level changes all the time.
An A1C test may be used to screen for or diagnose:

Type 2 diabetes. With type 2 diabetes your blood glucose gets too high.
Prediabetes. Prediabetes means that your blood glucose levels are higher than normal.

The A1C test isn't used to diagnose type 1 diabetes but may be used for monitoring your blood glucose levels.Why do I need an A1C test?
You may also need an A1C test if you have symptoms of diabetes, such as:

Feeling very thirsty
Urinating (peeing) a lot
What happens during an A1C test?
A health care professional will take a blood sample from a vein in your arm, using a small needle.What do the results mean?
A1C results tell you what percentage of your hemoglobin is coated with glucose. Ask your provider what A1C percentage is healthy for you.
To diagnose diabetes or prediabetes, the percentages commonly used are:

Normal: A1C below 5.7%
Prediabetes: A1C between 5.7% and 6.4%
Diabetes: A1C of 6.5% or higher

Providers often use more than one test to diagnose diabetes.
Learn more about laboratory tests, reference ranges, and understanding results.Is there anything else I need to know about an A1C test?
The A1C test is not used to diagnose gestational diabetes.References

American Diabetes Association [Internet]. Arlington (VA). Available from: https://www.diabetes.org/diabetes/A1C
